chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, by his chain, said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'All water is pure until it is known to be impure.'

key_terms.الماء: Water in Islamic jurisprudence, the medium for ritual purification
key_terms.طاهر: Ritually pure (tahir); legally valid for use in purification acts
key_terms.قذر: Impure, dirty (najis); water that has been contaminated and is no longer valid for purification

ai.seo_question: Is all water considered pure in Islam until proven otherwise?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational Islamic legal principle that water is presumed ritually pure by default, and this presumption holds until there is definite knowledge of its impurity. This ruling reflects the broader jurisprudential maxim of presumption of purity (istishab al-tahara) and has far-reaching implications for wudu, ghusl, and other acts of worship requiring pure water. The original audience — students of Shia fiqh — would have understood this as settling a fundamental question in ritual law.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn Al Lulu’ie, by his chain, said,
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The water, all of it is (to be considered as) clean, until one knows that it is dirty’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Hassan ibn al-Hassan al-Lu’lu’i through his chain of narrators has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘All water is clean until it is found out that it is not clean.”’
